statement: $ABCDEFGHI$ is a regular nine-sided polygon, with its vertices labelled in order. The diagonals $AD$ and $BF$ cross at the point $P$. What is the size of angle $APB$?

choices.misconception: I halved only the arc $AB$, $40^\circ$, and forgot the arc on the other side of $P$.
I halved only the arc $DF$, $80^\circ$, and forgot the arc $AB$.
I added the arcs $AB$ and $DF$, $40^\circ + 80^\circ$, but forgot to halve the total.
I assumed the angle between two diagonals equals an interior angle of the nonagon, $140^\circ$.

hints: Draw the circle through all nine vertices.
Each side of the nonagon cuts off an arc of $40^\circ$. Angles at a point on the circle are half the arc they stand on. Find two angles of triangle $ABP$ that way.

Angle $BAP$ is angle $BAD$, which stands on arc $BD$ (two sides, $80^\circ$), so it is $40^\circ$. Angle $ABP$ is angle $ABF$, which stands on arc $AF$ not containing $B$ (four sides, $160^\circ$), so it is $80^\circ$.

solutions.reliable: Put the nonagon in its circle; each side cuts off an arc of $360^\circ \div 9 = 40^\circ$. In triangle $ABP$, angle $BAP = \angle BAD$ stands on arc $BCD$ of $80^\circ$, so it is $40^\circ$. Angle $ABP = \angle ABF$ stands on arc $FGHIA$ of $160^\circ$, so it is $80^\circ$. Then angle $APB = 180^\circ - 40^\circ - 80^\circ = 60^\circ$. The transferable idea: in a regular polygon, every angle between vertices is a multiple of half the arc of one side.
solutions.elegant: Two chords crossing inside a circle make an angle equal to half the sum of the arcs they cut off. Angle $APB$ faces arc $AB$ ($40^\circ$) and its vertical angle faces arc $DF$ ($80^\circ$), so $APB = (40 + 80) \div 2 = 60^\circ$.

whyOnTest: Regular polygons live on a circle, and inscribed-angle facts turn any angle between diagonals into simple counting of sides.
